title: Rare-earth-free high-performance permanent magnets
bottleneck: The strongest permanent magnets need neodymium, dysprosium, or other rare earths with concentrated, geopolitically risky supply chains. Alternatives like manganese-bismuth, iron-nitride, or tetrataenite have promising anisotropy on paper but suffer from poor coercivity, thermal instability, or synthesis routes that do not scale. No rare-earth-free magnet yet matches NdFeB energy product at motor operating temperatures.
why_it_blocks: EV motors and wind turbine generators are the two largest growth markets for permanent magnets; rare-earth dependence exposes both to price shocks and export controls. Without an alternative, the energy transition's core machines stay hostage to a handful of suppliers.
current_state: Iron-nitride and manganese-based magnets keep improving in the lab, and dysprosium-free NdFeB grades have cut heavy-rare-earth use. But a true rare-earth-free drop-in replacement at NdFeB performance remains one of magnetics' grand challenges.
